title: Assasquage
summary: Assasquage is identified with Great Meadow Creek near Jamesport in Riverhead town. The name appears in a 1648 deed for the tract commonly called Ocquebauck, where planting land was reserved between Miamegg and Assasquage. The name is interpreted as a great grass place or great marshy place.
address_label: Great Meadow Creek / South Jamesport area, Riverhead, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern point in the South Jamesport / Great Meadow Creek area based on Tooker's identification; modern creek course remains uncertain.
why_this_matters: Assasquage preserves a Native name for Great Meadow Creek near Jamesport, interpreted as a great grass place or great meadow. The 1648 deed context connects the creek to nearby planting land, showing how waterways, meadow ecology, and cultivation were recorded together in colonial paperwork. Riverhead's creeks and meadows belong to Indigenous land relationships and foodways, not just background scenery.
translation_content:
Another recorded form is Assasquog, related to Massasquogue. The name is interpreted as a great grass place or great marshy place, meaning a great meadow.

Why Place Names Matter

“In the pressure of business, names were imperfectly heard and understood, and in the same record, perhaps in the same paragraph, may have several different forms.”

— William M. Beauchamp, Aboriginal Place Names of New York (1907), Printed p. 7; Internet Archive scan leaf n12

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: Assasquage links a creek, meadow, planting ground, and fishing place near Jamesport. The Native place name remains visible while the modern map point stays approximate until the historical creek course can be reviewed more closely.
